recipes.name: 15-Minute Dinner Nachos Supreme
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.12 ounce) package Pace® Taco Seasoning Mix
1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Tomato Soup

steps.text: Cook beef and taco seasoning in a skillet until browned. Pour off fat.
Add condensed soup, water, and rice. Heat to a boil. Cover and cook over low heat until rice is tender, about 5 min.
Top with salsa, Cheddar, and lettuce. Serve with tortilla chips for dipping.

raw_recipe.headline: 15-Minute Dinner Nachos Supreme
raw_recipe.description: Enjoy nachos for dinner with crisp tortilla chips dipped into tomatoey taco-seasoned ground beef and rice topped with salsa, cheese and lettuce.

review.reviewBody: Very yummy!! I did make some changes though. I used ground turkey instead of ground beef to make it a little healthier (next time I may use more than one pound). I also had to cook it for about 10 minutes in Step 2. After that, I poured the mixture into a casserole dish, covered it with some salsa, then with some sour cream, and finally I sprinkled some cheddar and mozzarella cheese on top. Then I popped in under the broiler for just a few minutes until the cheese was melted. We used the light restaurant-style tortilla chips and they were great. Both my husband and I loved it! We'll probably end up getting two or three meals out of it too. This is definitely going in my recipe box!

This was pretty good! I browned and drained the meat before I added the taco seasoning so I didn't pour any off with the fat. Then I added 1 1/2 c water, a can of tomato soup, an 8 oz can of tomato sauce, 1/2 jar of salsa. Then I added 1 cup of regular long grain rice. I let it all simmer covered for about 20 minutes and then stirred it up to get the rice off of the bottom. It was really good! The rice has so much more flavor and texture when you cook it with sauces and there was enough thickened liquid left over to give it a really nice sauce. I served it with lettuce, cheese and red onion. Super yum!

As written 3 stars but with these modifications 5 stars. I used ground turkey and made the rice separately and then added to the meat mixture. Then I added pinto beans, diced tomatoes, lettuce, olives and cheese and put it in the oven for 10 minutes and broiled it the last few minutes and it turned out amazing! Very tasty and the whole family loved it!

very easy and simple, of course I changed the whole recipe; I did spanish yellow goya rice(1 box) instead of plain white rice,used heinz chilli/ketchup sauce(it comes in like a bottle in ketchup aisle) for a little spice added just a little water to loosen the ketchupy flavor,added corn with cayenne pepper and parsley, and then turned it down low and sprinkled it with garlic powder and sargento's five cheese and let the cheese melt....so good with the salsa,of course i seperated the meat and salsa for people to add as they liked,it was so much i thought a pound wasnt going to be enough but once u add the rice trust me you can feed at least 5 very hugnry guys off that

I was planning to make this recipe as stated but ended up doing my own thing with this in mind. I made the meat as stated but added a can of Rotel's tomatoes & chiles to it. Instead of making my own rice, I bought Lipton's Spanish Rice- made as directed and then added it to the meat mixture. I also heated up a can of refried beans. I melted the cheese on the chips in the microwave first then added the beans and meat/rice mixture and topped with salsa, taco sauce & sour cream. Absolutely loved it!! It's like making your own Nacho Bellgrande :)

Living in a place where canned soup isn't available, I substituted a box of tomato sauce. After reading reviews, and not having instant rice at home, I cooked regular rice in the rice cooker. I also added corn. I decreased the water to 3/4 cups since it wouldn't be absorbed by the rice cooking. Good basic recipe to start with.

This is good, and my "meat, bread, and cheese only" husband likes it too. It's easy to make. The only reason I did not give it five stars is that there is nothing that makes it really stand out. I will be making it again regularly though I am sure.
I added some re-fried beans to it and put it all except the salsa and lettuce into a casserole dish. Put the chips on a cookie sheet and warmed them both in the oven for 6 mins.

At first I thought it was a dip. But when I made it, it was even better than that. I layered the chips in a Jelly Roll pan put the beef and rice mix on top, sprinkled it with cheese, and put it in the oven on broil for a couple minutes. It turned out awesome.

This made really good taco filling. It would be good for hard shell or soft shell taco dinners as well as presented as suggested. I added the seasoning (sorry, a homemade one from this site although I did use Pace salsa!) with everything else after draining off the fat so as not to lose all the flavor. Also topped with a mexican cheese blend instead of plain cheddar. One last thing, this recipe makes much more than 4 servings, unless you have BIG eaters.

This was an enjoyable summer meal. The only thing I changed was, after altering it for 2 persons, place a layer of Multi-grain Tostitos chips on the platter 1st, then a layer of the meat sauce, a layer of lettuce, a layer of salsa, cheese & repeated it over until pan was empty. Then I topped it off with sour cream. We had to serve it with a large spoon, but there were no leftovers.
Thanks!

Fast Easy Delicious!!! I picked up a box of mexican rice and made it while browning the beef. Added a can of diced tomotatoes. Combined the beef and rice, topped with shredded cheese, shredded lettuce, sour cream and guac. The kids loved scooping the mixture with tortilla chips!!! Very Yummy

Quick and easy! I was going to make this for my grandson’s birthday party and then the menu got changed. Since I already had the ingredients, I made it for dinner the next night. We put the mix in Old El Paso stand up taco shells. I only used 1/2 package seasoning and still delicious topped off with the toppings!

This is similar to Taco Bell nacho supreme but the original had beans as you stated then meat, nacho cheese, tomatoes ( not salsa) and sour cream. It also did not have rice. I worked as a training manager for TB in the 90's and somehow still remember all of the builds for a lot of their items. Actually my wife and I are having chili cheese burritos (or chilitos as they were known then) for supper tonight....YUMMERS.
Would have been better if I would have used instant rice.
Awesome easy way to make great Nachos. My family loved them.

I have made this recipe AS IS for several years now and have only just now changed it up. I love the original recipe like no other. but this time I added a can of tomatoes with green chilis and a can of corn. it just adds a little something extra. :)

I also love putting it in tortillas for burritos!

Yes it was okay. Needed a few extra goodies. I used onion and bell pepper, garlic salt and chili powder. And instead of cheddar cheese I used Velveeta and a can of Rotel Plus it needed more water and a few minutes longer to cook. Worth a try again..
I use this to make a burrito mix by adding black beans. Super tasty!

I think it was good but needed something more..
I think the next time i will tweek it a bit... 
Basimati Rice is the best rice ever so I will try that.
other than that pretty good.
Our families new favorite dinner! Easy to make and so customizable. Add sour cream, chipotle sauce, nacho cheese sauce or just leave as is.
